This sounds frustrating, but "no lights at all" usually points to a power supply issue rather than a complex mechanical failure. Let's troubleshoot step-by-step, starting with the most common causes.

### 🔌 Step 1: Check the Power Source (Most Common)
1. Unplug and Replug: Unplug the washer from the wall outlet. Wait 30 seconds, then plug it back in firmly. Sometimes a loose connection can cause this.
2. Check the Outlet: Plug another device (like a lamp or phone charger) into the same outlet to make sure it’s working.
• If the other device doesn’t work → The problem is with your home’s electrical system (tripped breaker, GFCI outlet, etc.).
3. Check for Tripped Breakers: Go to your home’s electrical panel and look for a tripped breaker (it will be in the middle or "off" position). Flip it fully off, then back on.
4. Check GFCI Outlets: If your washer is plugged into a bathroom, garage, or outdoor outlet, it might be protected by a GFCI outlet. Press the "Reset" button on that outlet.

### 🔌 Step 2: Inspect the Power Cord & Connection
1. Examine the Cord: Look for any visible damage, cuts, or chew marks (if you have pets).
2. Check the Plug: Make sure the plug is fully inserted into the wall outlet. Some washers require a heavy-duty outlet; if it’s loose, it may not make contact.

### 🚰 Step 3: Check for Water Inlet Issues (Less Likely to Cause No Power, But Possible)
• Water Shut-off Valves: Ensure both hot and cold water valves behind the washer are fully open. While this usually doesn’t prevent power-on, some models have safety sensors that may behave oddly if no water is detected.

### ⚠️ Step 4: Internal Issues (If Power Is Confirmed Good)
If you’ve confirmed the outlet works and the breaker hasn’t tripped, but there’s still no lights or response, the issue could be internal:
1. Door/Lid Switch: If the washer thinks the door is open, it won’t power on. Try closing the door firmly. Listen for a click. If the switch is broken, it may need replacement.
2. Control Board Failure: The electronic control board (the "brain" of the washer) may have failed. This is common in older models or after power surges.
3. Power Supply Module: Some washers have a separate module that converts household voltage to low voltage for the controls. If this fails, you’ll get no lights.

### 🛠️ What You Can Do Next:
1. Confirm Power: Use a multimeter or ask an electrician if you’re unsure about the outlet/breaker.
2. Reset the Washer: Unplug it for 5–10 minutes to reset any electronic glitches, then plug it back in.
3. Check for Error Codes: Some washers have a display that flashes even if lights are off (try shining a flashlight on the panel).
4. Call a Technician: If power is confirmed good and the washer still shows no signs of life, you likely need a professional to diagnose a failed control board or internal wiring issue.

### ❓ Questions to Help Narrow It Down:
• What brand and model is your washer?
• Did this happen suddenly, or was there a storm/power surge recently?
• Are any other appliances on the same circuit working?
• Does the washer make any sound (even a faint hum) when you press start?

Since you can't easily access the plug and the outlet is confirmed to be working (the kettle works), we need to look for other reasons why the machine isn't getting power. Here are a few things you can check without needing to move the appliance:

### 1. Check for a "Child Lock" or Control Lock
Many modern washers have a safety feature called Child Lock or Control Lock. When this is active, the display and buttons often go completely dark or unresponsive to prevent accidental changes.
• What to do: Look at your control panel for any icons that look like a lock 🔒 or say "CL" / "Lock." If you see one, try holding down two specific buttons simultaneously (often labeled together with a line between them) for 3–5 seconds until the light blinks off.

### 2. Check for a Tripped Residual Current Device (RCD)
You mentioned all switches at the fuse box are "up," but sometimes an RCD trips in a way that isn't immediately obvious on older panels, or it might be a separate switch entirely.
• What to do: Double-check your consumer unit (fuse box). Look for any small red or orange buttons that have popped out next to the switches. If you see one, press it back in before flipping the main switch.

### 3. Inspect the Power Cord at the Back
Even though you can't pull the washer out, try to look behind the cupboard door where the power cord enters the machine.
• What to do: Shine a flashlight into that gap. Look for:
• A loose plug in the socket (if it's a standard plug).
• A hardwired connection (a cable coming directly out of the wall with no plug) that might have come loose from its terminal block.

### 4. Check for a Built-in Fuse or Reset Button
Some washers, especially older models or those built into cupboards, have a small reset button or a fuse holder on the back panel near where the power cord enters.
• What to do: Look closely at the back of the machine (as far as you can see) for a small red or black button labeled "Reset" or a small socket that might hold a fuse.

### 5. Consider a Power Surge or Internal Fuse Blow
If there was a recent power surge, the internal fuse on the washer's circuit board may have blown. This is common if other appliances in your kitchen also acted up recently.
• What to do: Unfortunately, this requires opening the back panel of the washer, which should be done by a qualified appliance repair technician for safety reasons.

### Next Steps:
Since you can't access the plug and the power seems good elsewhere, I recommend:
1.  Try the Child Lock reset first (it's the easiest fix).
2.  If that doesn't work, try to find the brand name on the inside of the door frame or on the control panel edge. Even if it's worn off, there might be a model number sticker nearby. This will help you look up specific troubleshooting steps for your machine.
3.  If none of this works, you'll likely need an appliance repair technician to check the internal power supply unit (PSU) or main board.

### 1. Check for a "Delay Start" or Timer Issue
Sometimes, if a timer is set incorrectly or a delay start was accidentally activated, the machine won't power on until that time elapses.
• What to do: Try turning the dial or pressing buttons to see if you can reset the cycle. Sometimes just turning the main knob all the way around and back to "Off" can clear a stuck state.

### 2. Listen for a Hum or Click
Even though there are no lights, try starting a cycle and listening very closely at the front of the machine.
• What to do: Turn it on and listen for any faint hum from the motor or a click from the relay. If you hear a hum but nothing else happens, it might be a different issue than a total power loss.

### 3. Check the Water Supply Valves
While this usually doesn't cause a "no power" issue, some modern machines have safety sensors that prevent them from starting if they don't detect water pressure immediately.
• What to do: Make sure both the hot and cold water taps behind the cupboard are fully turned on.

### 4. Look for a Reset Button or Fuse Holder
Some washers have a small reset button or a fuse holder located on the front panel, often near the power cord entry point (if visible).
• What to do: Shine a flashlight into any gaps around the control panel or where the power cord enters the machine.

### 5. Consider the Age and Type of Machine
